meta.description: Quran recitation, dua and live ilahi — then a full dance floor. One running order, one PA, one point of contact. Stuttgart and across Germany.

hero.title: The dua and the dance floor, same evening
hero.subtitle: Quran recitation, dua and ilahi belong in the running order here, not in a separate booking. The celebration starts afterwards — both from one supplier, hosted in German, Turkish and English.

intro.title: Can the two actually go together?
intro.body: Almost every couple is handed two separate quotes at this point — one for the religious part, one for the party — and has to organise the transitions themselves. That is exactly where the evening tips over: the music is cut mid-track, nobody knows when guests are meant to sit down, and after the dua the room simply stalls. Here both are a single running order, written by the person who also runs it on the night.

recitation.title: I recite the tilawet myself
recitation.body: The Quran recitation does not come from a recording, and not from an outside guest squeezed in between two other bookings: Veysel Durmuş recites it himself. In practice that means recitation, dua, ilahi, hosting and the DJ set all sit with one person — so the transition from the last word to the first announcement stops being a risk and becomes part of the plan.

program.title: What the evening is made of
program.lead: Freely combinable. In the planning call we decide which of these belong to your celebration — and which explicitly do not.

tilawet.title: Quran recitation
tilawet.text: Recited live, on its own microphone, without reverb or effects and at a markedly lower level than the dance set. Intelligibility everywhere in the room is the only goal.

dua.title: Dua
dua.text: Given a fixed slot in the running order, usually before dinner or before the first dance. A bilingual announcement first, so every guest knows what is about to happen.

ilahi.title: Ilahi — live
ilahi.text: Performed live, with saz accompaniment on request. No playback, no playlist.

tsm.title: Türk Sanat Müziği
tsm.text: Usually during dinner or as a calmer block between two dance rounds — also possible live on the saz rather than only off a laptop.

djset.title: DJ set & hosting
djset.text: Turkish, German and international music blended rather than played in separate blocks. Hosting live in German, Turkish and English.

afterparty.title: After-wedding party
afterparty.text: The more informal part once the official programme is over — or a separate date in a smaller circle, before or after.

timeline.title: How an evening like this actually runs
timeline.lead: A pattern from practice. Times, order and the length of each block shift with your venue and your guest count.
timeline.note: This running order is an example, not an offer. Your real one comes out of the planning call and is then written into the contract.

bio.short: Veysel Durmuş has spent over 12 years as a DJ, musician and host for German-Turkish, Turkish and multicultural weddings and events. He has accompanied more than 200 celebrations, performed live on saz and guitar, and hosted trilingually in German, Turkish and English.
long: Veysel Durmuş has played saz and guitar since childhood — music was never just a hobby, but a means of expression from the start. Today he brings that ear for sound and timing to German-Turkish, Turkish and multicultural weddings and events as a DJ, live musician and host, with over 12 years and more than 200 celebrations behind him.

By day he works as an IT specialist (Informatiker) — the precision and planning discipline from that profession carries straight into every event: a considered run of show, clean technology, no surprises.

Off duty he's a marathon runner and triathlete. It's not unusual for him to run 10 kilometres on the morning of a wedding, to step onto the dance floor that evening full of energy. After the wedding season, he recharges by camping in the Alps.
His own words put it best: “My goal isn't just to play music. My goal is to create emotions.” And: “Only someone who is full of energy themselves can pass that energy on to others.”

intent.title: Even without a city name: the right answers

items.q: Is there a Turkish wedding DJ who books Germany-wide?
items.a: Yes. DJ Veys is based in Stuttgart and Baden-Württemberg and books Germany-wide — from Munich to Hamburg. Travel and equipment are calculated individually per location in the quote; hosting stays the same everywhere: German, Turkish, English.

items.q: Can I book a wedding DJ for a destination wedding abroad?
items.a: Yes. Five countries are prepared in depth — Austria, Switzerland, the Netherlands, Belgium, France — each with its own travel logistics and technical specifics. Other European countries are bookable too, with travel calculated individually.

items.q: Is there a DJ for a Turkish wedding abroad?
items.a: Yes, that's one of the core strengths: German-Turkish, purely Turkish and multicultural weddings outside Germany, with Halay, live-orchestra elements and trilingual hosting — the same standard as in Stuttgart, just with travel itemised separately in the quote.

items.q: How far do you travel for weddings?
items.a: Within the core radius around Stuttgart, travel is usually included; enquiries arrive regularly from across Germany and Europe, and we are bookable there just the same. Distance affects lead time and cost, not willingness.

countries.title: Written in depth, not templated
countries.subtitle: Each country with its own travel logistics, its own technical specifics and its own diaspora angle — deliberately not city pages, see the FAQ below.

more.title: More countries bookable Europe-wide
more.text: The following countries don't have a dedicated page yet — they're still bookable, with the same care. Travel, accommodation and equipment are itemised in your individual quote. For destinations outside the EU customs union (e.g. Norway, like Switzerland), equipment clearance adds an extra step via an ATA Carnet — that's factored into the quote too.

languages.title: Which languages are actually hosted live
languages.text: Live hosting is in German, Turkish and English — in every country listed here, regardless of the national language. This site exists in several languages so as many couples as possible can read it and get in touch; that's a different thing from the language spoken on the wedding night itself.

items.q: Why aren't there dedicated pages for individual European cities?
items.a: Because local Google results require proximity and a Google Business Profile in that area — neither of which a Stuttgart-based provider has in Oslo or Amsterdam. Country pages with real, distinct content are more honest and actually work; dozens of near-identical city pages would be exactly what Google's spam policies define as doorway pages.

items.q: How far in advance should I enquire for a wedding abroad?
items.a: As early as possible — travel and accommodation planning need more lead time than a celebration in Stuttgart. A first, no-obligation enquiry is possible at any time, even months ahead.

Always itemised individually and transparently in your quote: mileage or a flight for lightweight gear, accommodation, and — for destinations outside the EU customs union (e.g. Switzerland, Norway) — an extra customs step for the equipment via an ATA Carnet.

items.q: Do you also play countries not listed here?
items.a: Yes. The five featured countries are prepared in the most depth; other European destinations are generally bookable too, with travel calculated individually.
